title: Translational MicroRNA research in COVID-19: bridging in Silico prediction with clinical biomarker potential.
authors: El Sharkawi, Fathia Z; Mohamed, Marwa A; Montasser, Karim; Mahdi, Mamdouh M; Atya, Hanaa B
one_liner_zh: 该研究聚焦COVID-19中miRNA作为生物标志物的实验验证，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: COVID-19 continues to evolve. Thus, new therapeutic alternatives are needed. Some in silico analyses, including the role of microRNAs, have shown promising results, but they are based on computational simulations and predictions, so their consistency with real-world results may vary. This study investigated the potential of three miRNAs (miR-196a-5p, miR-98-5p, and miR-27a-3p) obtained from published bioinformatics results as promising biomarkers for different aspects of COVID-19 (susceptibility, severity, and therapeutic possibilities). The current study found that, serum levels of these miRNAs were significantly elevated in COVID-19 patients compared to healthy controls, particularly during the third wave patients which is contrast to that reported in In silico study regarding miR-98-5p. Additionally, serum levels of inflammatory markers such as interleukin - 6 (IL-6) and hypoxia inducible factor- 1 alpha (HIF-1alpha) were higher in patients compared to healthy control. miR-196a-5p exhibited high sensitivity and specificity for COVID-19 diagnosis. Finally, we highlight the necessity of validating microRNAs in patient serum, as our findings show that their differential expression is robust and independent of the initial predictive model. This study effectively translates a bioinformatics hypothesis into a verifiable biomarker through experimental validation regardless of the contradictory findings between hypothesis and the actual results.
abstract_zh: COVID-19持续演变，因此需要新的治疗选择。一些计算机模拟分析，包括microRNAs的作用，已显示出有前景的结果，但这些分析基于计算模拟和预测，因此其与现实世界结果的一致性可能有所不同。本研究调查了从已发表的生物信息学结果中获得的三种miRNAs（miR-196a-5p、miR-98-5p和miR-27a-3p）作为COVID-19不同方面（易感性、严重性和治疗可能性）潜在生物标志物的可能性。本研究发现，与健康对照组相比，COVID-19患者血清中这些miRNAs的水平显著升高，尤其是在第三波患者中，这与计算机模拟研究中关于miR-98-5p的报告相反。此外，与健康对照组相比，患者血清中炎症标志物如白细胞介素-6（IL-6）和缺氧诱导因子-1α（HIF-1alpha）的水平更高。miR-196a-5p在COVID-19诊断中表现出高敏感性和特异性。最后，我们强调在患者血清中验证microRNAs的必要性，因为我们的研究结果表明，它们的差异表达是稳健的，且独立于初始预测模型。本研究通过实验验证，有效地将生物信息学假设转化为可验证的生物标志物，尽管假设与实际结果之间存在矛盾发现。
